title: The HBB Mutation Spectrum and Organ-Specific Iron Loading in Bulgarian Children with Transfusion-Dependent β-Thalassemia: A Single-Center Exploratory Study
content: Objective: To characterize the HBB mutation spectrum in a contemporary Bulgarian pediatric cohort with transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia (TDT) and to explore genotype–phenotype relationships, including organ-specific iron loading by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) T2*. Materials and Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 37 children and adolescents with TDT receiving regular red-cell transfusions and iron chelation. HBB variants identified by Sanger sequencing and multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification were classified as β0, β+, or β++. Patients with two identified alleles were grouped by predicted genotype severity. Pretransfusion hemoglobin, serum ferritin, and cardiac, hepatic, and pancreatic MRI T2* were evaluated. All comparisons were exploratory. Results: Molecular characterization was available in 28 of 37 patients: 26 had a complete two-allele genotype and 2 had a single identified allele. Among these 28 genetically informative patients, 54 alleles were identified. IVS-I-110 predominated (18/54; 33.3%), followed by IVS-I-6 (13.0%), IVS-II-745 (13.0%), and FS5 (11.1%). Pretransfusion hemoglobin and serum ferritin did not differ significantly among genotype-severity groups (p=0.208 and p=0.289). Hepatic T2* was <6.3 ms in 9/14 patients and cardiac T2* was <20 ms in 2/19. Pancreatic T2* was ≤2.4 ms in all 7 patients examined, a small and possibly selected subgroup. Conclusion: The mutation spectrum closely reflects the established Bulgarian profile. Under regular transfusion therapy, broad genotype-severity categories were not reflected by pretransfusion hemoglobin or serum ferritin, whereas MRI demonstrated organ-specific heterogeneity. The pancreatic findings are preliminary and require prospective confirmation.
